package_info.package_manager: N/A (malicious DLL sideloaded via legitimate application)
package_info.why_malicious: The attack leverages DLL sideloading to inject a banking trojan (Casbaneiro) into legitimate business applications, enabling credential and credit card theft. The malicious DLL is delivered via trusted channels (Amazon AWS, GitHub), making detection difficult and allowing the attacker to steal sensitive user data.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the legitimate application loads the DLL)
execution_context.file_location: Malicious DLL placed in the same directory as the legitimate application executable

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malicious DLL is loaded by the legitimate application, executes credential and credit card theft routines, and exfiltrates the stolen data to a remote command-and-control server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: DLLs loaded by trusted applications should not perform credential or credit card theft, nor should they communicate with external servers to exfiltrate sensitive data.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal DLLs provide legitimate functionality to the host application; this DLL abuses the trust relationship to perform malicious actions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate DLLs may access user data for application functionality, but never for exfiltration to unauthorized servers.
key_indicators: DLL loaded from application directory instead of system path
Network communication to external C2 servers
Credential and credit card data access routines

attack_chain.action: Attacker delivers a legitimate business application bundled with a malicious DLL via trusted channels (Amazon AWS, GitHub).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious DLL is placed in the same directory as the application.

attack_chain.action: User executes the legitimate application, which loads the malicious DLL via DLL sideloading.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code in the DLL is executed in the context of the trusted application.

attack_chain.action: Malicious DLL steals login credentials and credit card information from the user.
attack_chain.leads_to: Stolen data is prepared for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Malicious DLL exfiltrates the stolen data to the attacker's command-and-control server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive user data (final goal).

behavioral_signatures: DLL loaded from application directory instead of system path
Unexpected network connections from business applications to unknown domains
Credential or credit card data access by DLLs not part of the application's normal operation
file_indicators: Presence of unsigned or suspicious DLLs in the same directory as trusted application executables
DLLs with recent creation dates or mismatched version information
network_indicators: Outbound connections to attacker-controlled domains or IPs (often hosted on AWS or GitHub)
Unusual data exfiltration patterns from business applications
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for DLLs loaded from the application directory that are not part of the official software package, especially if unsigned or recently added. Analyze network traffic from business applications for connections to unknown or suspicious domains. Use endpoint detection to flag processes that access credential stores or credit card data and attempt to send this information externally.
